content:
Appendix IV
EXCERPTS FROM SAME TEXT ŚAŃKU-STHĀPANĀ
(9th Patala)
शङ्‌कुच्छायाविधानेन वक्ष्ये प्राचीं विनिश्चिताम्।
देवविप्रनृपादीनां गृहारम्भविधेः पुरा ।॥१॥
उत्तरायणकाले तु शुक्लपक्षे शुभे दिने ।
यजमानानुकूलक्षं शिल्पिना सह देशिकः ॥२॥
विमले भ्युदयात्पूर्वे स्थापयेच्छङ्‌कुमुत्तमम्।
गृहीतवास्तुनो मध्ये दण्डमात्रं तु भूतलम् ॥३॥
समं कृत्वा जलेनैव कृत्वा दर्पणवत्सुधीः।
तन्मध्ये लक्षणोपेतं तस्य लक्षणमुच्यते ॥४॥
चतुर्विशाङ्गुलोत्सेधं वरं तस्य प्रकल्पयेत्।
षडङ्‌‌गुलक्षये तस्मिन्मध्यमोत्सेध उच्यते ॥५॥
तस्मात्षडङ्‌गुले हीने कन्यसोच्छ्रय उच्यते।
आयामसदृशं नाहं मूलेनास्य प्रयोजयेत् ॥ ६ ।।
ततिभागैकभागेन शिरोनाहः प्रकीर्तितः ।
शङ्‌कुमानेन तद्वाह्ये परितो मण्डलं लिखेत्॥७॥

Appendix IV ♦ 107
मण्डलत्रितयं चैव कृत्वा सूत्रेण संमितम्।
पूर्वापराह्णयोश्छायां प्रवेशे चाथ निर्गमे ॥८ ॥
छायाग्रयोगवृत्तेषु लक्षयित्वात्र लाञ्छयेत्।
पूर्वपश्चिमभागेषु मण्डलत्रयसंस्थिताः ॥९॥
छायाकारा भवन्त्यत्र तानाश्रित्य च संस्थिताः ।
पूर्वापरायता रेखास्तिस्त्रः कुर्याद्यथाक्रमम् ॥१०॥
मण्डलाध्यधिके ह्रासो न्यूने वृद्धिर्यथा भवेत्।
कारयित्वा तथा धीमान्मध्यवृत्तस्य मध्यगम् ‌११॥
पूर्वापरायतामेकां रेखां तदनुसारतः ।
तन्मण्डलप्रमाणेन सूत्रेण सुमितं ततः ॥१२॥
पूर्वपश्चिमपर्यन्त स्थितं पार्श्वक्रमेण तु ।
दक्षिणोत्तरगं मत्स्यं जनयित्वा तथा पुनः॥१३॥
पार्श्वयोरपि तन्मानात्पूर्वपश्चिमयोरपि ।
मत्स्यद्वयं पश्चात्प्राङ्मुखेषु च ॥१५॥
तेनैव चतुरश्रेण प्रासादं त्वत्र कारयेत्॥१७॥
summary: This appendix presents an excerpt from the 9th chapter (Patala) of a Sanskrit text on the topic of Śaṅku-Sthāpanā, which is the architectural procedure for establishing a gnomon to determine the cardinal directions. The text details the auspicious timing for this ritual, the precise dimensions of the gnomon (śaṅku), and the geometric method of using the gnomon's shadow to draw an East-West line. It then describes how to derive the North-South line using a compass-and-string method known as the 'matsya' (fish) figure. The ultimate goal is to correctly orient a building, such as a temple (prāsāda), by establishing a true square or rectangular (caturaśra) ground plan.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to provide a primary source text illustrating the traditional Indian astronomical and architectural method for determining the cardinal directions, specifically the East, before commencing the construction of a building. It serves as a practical guide from a Vastu Shastra text on the essential preliminary step of site orientation.
key_information: The text is about Śaṅku-Sthāpanā (the establishment of the gnomon).
It is a procedure to determine the East direction (prācī) for construction (gṛhārambha).
The ritual should be performed at an auspicious time: during Uttarāyaṇa (the sun's northern course), in a bright lunar fortnight (śuklapakṣa), on a favorable day.
The ground must be perfectly leveled ('like a mirror').
Three hierarchical heights (utsedha) for the gnomon are specified: 24 aṅgulas (best), 18 aṅgulas (medium), and 12 aṅgulas (inferior).
The method involves drawing circles (maṇḍala) and marking the points where the tip of the gnomon's shadow touches the circle in the morning and afternoon.
A line connecting these two points establishes the East-West axis (pūrvāparāyatā rekhā).
From the East-West line, the North-South axis is determined by constructing a 'matsya' (fish-like geometric figure formed by two intersecting arcs).
Once the directions are fixed, a square or rectangular (caturaśra) foundation for a building (prāsāda) can be laid out.

tables_and_data.data_summary: The text specifies three hierarchical sizes for the gnomon's height (उत्सेध) based on a unit of 'aṅgula': 'Best' (वरं) is 24 aṅgulas, 'Medium' (मध्यम) is 18 aṅgulas (a reduction of 6), and 'Inferior' (कन्यस) is 12 aṅgulas (a further reduction of 6).
